title: Rectangle sign has absolute value one
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic Boolean two-party communication protocol on input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob), and let $R \subseteq X \times Y$ be any set. Define the rectangle sign of $p$ on $R$ to be $+1$ when $p$ outputs $\mathrm{false}$ at every point of $R$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then the rectangle sign has absolute value $1$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a Boolean protocol on input types X and Y
R is a subset of X × Y
replaced: For any protocol $p$ and any set $R$, $|\mathrm{rectangleSign}(p,R)| = 1$.
